messages:
lee: Quick report: ran into a confusing auth case in sample-app. My shell has REDWOOD_ORG_KEY, repo has a checked-in .env with REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, and the SDK ended up sending both headers which triggered a mid-stream 401 and restarted the chat.

maya: Oof. Do we have a consistent precedence across SDKs? Node and Python have been diverging.

dom: Not yet. Proposal: explicit SDK param > CLI flag > REDWOOD_ORG_KEY env > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY env (unless REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true) > credential helpers/netrc > legacy. Defaulting org above project avoids CI surprises.

lee: Sounds reasonable. Small DX asks: 1) SDK should never emit multiple auth headers; pick one and drop the rest, 2) emit a single rate-limited WARN at startup when multiple sources detected, and 3) add a `redwood auth inspect` dry-run CLI so devs can see which source would win without making requests.

maya: Love the auth inspect idea. Also add `--auth-source` CLI pin for CI. And include a DEV-only header `X-Auth-Resolved: org|project|cred-helper` when REDWOOD_DEV_HEADERS=true to help staging triage (no secrets).

dom: For streaming recovery: on 401 attempt onAuthRefresh hook to swap token in-flight and retry frames; only close the user-level stream if refresh fails. Also invalidate netrc/cred-manager cache once on 401 to handle rotation.

infra-bot: note: ticket DEVEX-9002 created: "Auth inspect CLI + single-header enforcement + stream refresh hook".

lee: I'll open a tiny RFC + sample-app PR to remove checked-in .env and add .env.example with repro steps. I'll include the warn text and rate-limit guidance. Thanks all!
